text: Session-only activity feed, derived from the undo stack: what changed and when, in this tab. The project load resets the stack, so it is empty after every reload — not persisted, not per user.
Cap 50. Auto-saves prune oldest-first; named versions never prune. Approval is not tracked per version, so it protects nothing — do not imply it does.
Ctrl+Shift+T turns the list into a scrubber over the undo stack, showing each entry's label. The canvas does NOT change while scrubbing — no version carries a visual snapshot. Only Restore writes.
Your current work is saved as a version first. Pages, styles and brand settings are replaced — content records, media and saved components are not.

Restore always confirms and always saves the current state as a version first. It replaces pages, styles and brand settings; content records, media and saved components are untouched — so “nothing is lost” would be too strong.
Two independent panes. Left is the approved snapshot, right is the site as it is now. Each pane is a sandboxed frame and they scroll separately — the labels carry the asymmetry, not colour.

One pane. The current page is blended over the approved one and a slider moves between them, so a change reads as a shift when you scrub. Nothing is tinted or outlined — the frames are sandboxed and cannot be marked up.

Scoped runs edit only the selection — but page settings (title, description, slug) and a publish request are not element edits and can still come back. Clearing the selection widens the scope to the page.
Nothing was changed. Daily limit reached (10). Resets at midnight UTC.
Out of credit, and it says nothing was changed — the first question anyone asks when a run dies mid-way. The limit is DAILY (Free 10 / Pro 200), resetting at midnight UTC, not monthly.

AI proposes a diff for anything you ask it to change — alt text for a new image is the one exception, written automatically. Each Apply lands as one undo step; a multi-step draft applies one step at a time.
No records published yet. Dynamic pages generate only from published records — and only once a template page is bound.

🔗 chip in the header; bound fields go read-only with the collection and field named, plus an unbind action. A field that silently refuses typing is a bug report. Two things this state does not say: a binding to a DRAFT record publishes that draft's text, and publishing a record does not refresh the canvas.
